record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.original_question: Find a system of invariants that classifies isomorphism classes of genus-3 hyperelliptic curves, equivalently a set of invariants that separates points of the genus-3 hyperelliptic moduli space.

evidence.quote: In other words, there is no known way of identifying isomorphism classes of hyperelliptic curves of genus g >= 3.
Problem 14. Find invariants which classify the isomorphism classes of genus 3 hyperelliptic curves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A smooth projective curve $C$ of genus $3$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ is called hyperelliptic if it admits a degree-$2$ morphism to $\mathbb{P}^1$; equivalently (in characteristic $\neq 2$), it can be written as $y^2 = f(x)$ for a separable polynomial $f \in k[x]$ of degree $7$ or $8$. Two such curves are isomorphic if and only if the corresponding binary octic forms (obtained by homogenizing $f$) are equivalent under the natural action of $\mathrm{GL}_2(k)$.

Determine an explicit finite system of invariants $I_1, \ldots, I_n$ (polynomial/rational functions in the coefficients of the defining binary form, invariant under the $\mathrm{GL}_2$-action) such that the tuple $(I_1(C), \ldots, I_n(C))$ classifies the isomorphism class of a genus-$3$ hyperelliptic curve $C$; equivalently, exhibit a set of invariants that separates the points of the coarse moduli space of genus-$3$ hyperelliptic curves.
artifact.category_tag: Moduli of hyperelliptic curves / invariants of binary forms
artifact.status_search_result: The Shioda invariants $J_2, J_3, \ldots, J_{10}$ of binary octic forms classify isomorphism classes of genus-$3$ hyperelliptic curves in characteristic $0$ or $p > 7$. Explicit algorithms (Lercier–Ritzenthaler and others) compute these invariants and reconstruct curves from them. In small positive characteristics ($p = 3, 5, 7$), additional invariants have been described to complete the classification. Thus the problem is solved.

status_evidence.title: Hyperelliptic curves and their invariants: geometric, arithmetic and algorithmic aspects
status_evidence.snippet: Shioda invariants classify hyperelliptic curves of genus 3 up to isomorphism in characteristic 0 and p > 7; supplementary invariants are given in small characteristic.
status_evidence.claim: Genus-3 hyperelliptic curves admit a complete classification by Shioda invariants (plus extras in small characteristic).

status_evidence.title: Isomorphism classes of hyperelliptic curves of genus 3 over finite fields
status_evidence.snippet: Provides invariants and counts for isomorphism classes of genus 3 hyperelliptic curves over finite fields.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit invariants separating isomorphism classes have been worked out.

status_evidence.title: Modular invariants for genus 3 hyperelliptic curves
status_evidence.snippet: Connections between invariants of binary octics and Siegel modular forms classify the hyperelliptic locus in genus 3.
status_evidence.claim: Modular and algebraic invariants together classify genus-3 hyperelliptic curves.
